annotations.title: Read a file onto a declared format

description: Read what the user already keeps onto a declared format: any .csv, .xlsx (or .xls) or .json of rows, a file row per table row; or **a folder of Markdown notes**, a note per row: `title`, `file`, each frontmatter key, `inline tags`, `body links` and `body`, with a link read from `[[name]]` or `[text](file.md)`; a body link naming no row is left out and named, the note still read; a hidden file is not read; links between notes of one folder are filled; `items` reads list items or table rows onto another format, each linked to its note. **Dry-runs by default**: the reader with each key’s header cell and first value, the rows as stored, the rows that would not type and why, and **what the format claims, checked before a row exists**. Writes on `commit: true`. Keys come from `formats`. **The user maps the columns; this only guesses** — show the reader, correct it with `columns`. `fixed` gives a key one value for the file (a currency, a unit, the row every line belongs to). A column fills a `link` only by the exact unique name of its row, and a line naming none is refused; a link is guessed only from a header that names it. `header` writes the file’s total, period or card as one row of another format that every line links to. **A source read again updates its rows** by note file name, and any file by a unique column (so a later export updates what an earlier one wrote): changed, added and gone named; gone kept unless `remove_gone`. `supersede_reading` takes a reading back. **Several files in one call**: `files`, each `{ file, format }` with its own columns — read in the order their links need, so a line names a row from a file above it; one dry run for the lot, written whole or not at all.

columns.description: Column number → key of the format, from what the user confirmed, or → null to read nothing from that column. Applied over the reader the dry run showed, so send only what changes; a column not named keeps its key. Omit to take the guess, or the reading this document already has for a file with this header.

commit.description: Write it. Omit or false for the dry run.

date_order.description: How a written date is ordered: one of dmy, mdy, ymd. Inferred from the file when omitted.

file.description: Absolute path to the file to read: one of .xlsx, .xls, .csv, a .json file of rows (an array of objects, or an object holding one), a Markdown note (.md), or **a folder of notes** — every .md file in it is one row, and a hidden one (a name starting with a dot) none.

files.description: Instead of `format` and `file`: each `{ file, format }`, plus that file’s own columns.

fixed.description: Key → one value for every row of this file. A currency for a `money` column, a unit for a `quantity` one, or the row a `link` points at, by id or unique name.

format.description: The declared format to read onto, by name. Not with `files`.

header.description: `{ format, link, cells, fixed }`: the one row of another format this file writes and every line links to through `link`. `cells` is key → [row, column], **a position, never a value**, from 0; a negative row counts up from the last row with anything (a total under the lines is `[-1, 0]`). An aggregate and a claim there check it.

header_row.description: Force the header row, from 0, when the guess is wrong — exports often have a preamble.

items.description: "list" or "table": a folder’s list items or table rows as rows of `format`, each linked to its note’s row (read the notes in the same `files`, or before).

path.description: Absolute path to a .emd file on this machine.

recursive.description: A folder of notes: its subfolders’ notes too (not a hidden one), with a `folder` column, the path under it.

remove_gone.description: Read again: remove rows whose line is gone (else named, kept). Per file in `files`.

separators.description: Key → what splits one cell into several members, for a column holding several of a list (`enums`): `{ "tags": "," }` reads `vegan, quick` as two. Never guessed; without one a cell is one member, and a member off the list refuses its line by name.

sheet.description: Which sheet, or key of a .json object; defaults to the first.

under.description: With `items`: only those under this heading.

name: read_onto_format
title: Read a file onto a declared format
